After months of testing, Apple today officially launched Siri AI to the public, as part of iOS 27 and other operating system updates.

During the setup process, users will see a new prompt asking whether they would like to opt in to help improve Siri and Apple Intelligence. Here's what this option means.

Prior to today, users were asked during setup whether they wanted to help improve Siri and Dictation. If they chose to opt in, audio and text transcripts of Siri and Dictation interactions would be shared with Apple.

Starting today, when users enable Siri AI, they will see a setup screen asking whether they would like to opt in to "Improve Siri & Apple Intelligence," with two options: "Share Audio & Text" or "Not Now."

Apple's explanation is as follows:

Improve Siri & Apple Intelligence — Allow Apple to collect and use text and audio interactions you have with Siri, Dictation, and Translate to help improve the underlying foundation models and Siri.

It's worth noting that if you opt in to this setting, the type of data Apple collects has not actually changed. What has changed is that Apple will now use this data to train and improve its foundation models, in addition to using it as always to improve Siri and Dictation.

Even users who previously opted in under the old settings will be asked again when they enable Siri AI. This gives them the opportunity to reassess their choice, as this data will now also be used to train Apple's foundation models.

Apple has made clear the privacy safeguards in place when asking users to opt in. The company says that Siri audio data, text transcripts, and related data are tied to a "randomly generated device identifier that changes frequently, often multiple times per hour," and are not linked to your Apple Account or email address. Apple also does not use this data to build marketing profiles, nor does it sell it to anyone.

You can turn this option on or off at any time via Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements > Improve Siri & Apple Intelligence.

Apple has also published a new support document detailing how these settings apply across platforms.
